q: 1. Lime mortar is generally made with ............
explain: Hydraulic lime is preferred for mortar because it has the property of setting under water or in thick walls where air circulation is limited, making it suitable for structural masonry.

q: 2. The commonly used lime in white-washing, is ............
explain: Fat lime (also known as rich lime or white lime) is used for white-washing and plastering because it slakes vigorously, has high plasticity, and provides a smooth, white finish.

q: 3. Lime concrete is generally used for ............
explain: Lime concrete provides a good base for foundations and ground floors due to its durability and resistance to subsoil dampness.But as per Book Key b is answer

q: 4. The minimum percentage of silica, alumina and ferric oxide in lime for white washing, is ............
explain: Lime used for white-washing (Fat Lime) should be as pure as possible (high calcium oxide content), meaning the percentage of impurities like silica, alumina, and iron oxide should ideally be zero.

q: 5. The initial setting time of hydraulic lime, is ............
explain: Unlike cement, hydraulic lime sets much slower. Its initial setting time is generally taken as 120 minutes (2 hours).

q: 6. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolona, is ............
explain: The addition of pozzolana to lime influences the setting properties, but the standard initial setting time for this mix is also categorized at 120 minutes.

q: 7. The steel used for the manufacture of rails, is ............
explain: Rails require steel that is hard and wear-resistant. Bessemer steel, often high-carbon, is historically used for rail manufacturing.

q: 8. Which of the following is a rock?
explain: Quartz and Mica are minerals. Gypsum is a sedimentary rock (evaporite) consisting of calcium sulfate dihydrate.

q: 9. Which of the following metamorphic rocks has the most weather resisting characteristics?
explain: Quartzite is a very hard, non-foliated metamorphic rock which was originally pure quartz sandstone. Its mineral composition makes it highly resistant to chemical and physical weathering.

q: 10. A good building stone should not absorb water more than ............
explain: For a stone to be considered high quality for construction, its water absorption should be less than 5% by weight. Above 10%, the stone is generally rejected.

q: 11. Which of the following has more fire resisting characteristics?
explain: Compact sandstone is better at resisting fire compared to others because its grain structure doesn't disintegrate as easily under high heat as marble or granite.

q: 12. Jumper is a tool used for ............
explain: A jumper is a long steel bar used in quarrying to drill deep holes in rocks for blasting.

q: 13. The important test to be conducted on a stone used in docks and harbours is ............
explain: Stones used in docks and harbours must be heavy to resist the force of waves and water pressure; therefore, the weight (specific gravity) test is critical.

q: 14. The filler used in plastic bitumen, is ............
explain: Asbestos powder is used as a filler in bitumen to improve its temperature resistance and binding properties for certain industrial applications.

q: 15. Igneous rock has ............
options: foliated structure which is hard and durable
layers of different composition, colour and structure
explain: Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling of magma or lava, resulting in a crystalline or glassy texture. They do not have layers (stratification) or foliation.

q: 16. Gneiss is chemically classified as ............
explain: Gneiss is a silicious rock as its main constituent is silica (quartz). It is formed by the metamorphosis of granite.

q: 17. Marble is an example of ............
explain: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from the recrystallization of limestone or dolomite under heat and pressure.

q: 18. The curved swellings from the growth of layers or wounds left after branches are cut off in an irregular manner are known as ............
explain: Rindgalls are curved swellings that form over a wound or where a branch has been improperly removed from a tree.

q: 19. The burning of bricks in kilns is complete within ............ hours.
explain: The actual burning process in a kiln typically takes about 24 hours (one full day) to reach the required temperature and complete the chemical transformation of clay.

q: 20. The bricks after burning in kilns require about ............ days to cool down for unloading.
explain: Sudden cooling makes bricks brittle. To maintain quality, they are allowed to cool gradually for about 12 days before unloading.

q: 21. The bricks should be burnt at temperature from ............
explain: Bricks must be burnt between 1000°C and 1200°C to achieve vitrification. Below 1000°C, they remain soft; above 1200°C, they may melt and distort.

q: 22. The type of brick suitable for panel walls for multi-storeyed buildings is ............
explain: Both hollow and perforated bricks are used in high-rise panel walls to reduce the dead weight of the structure and provide better thermal insulation.

q: 23. The compressive strength of perforated bricks should not be less than ............
explain: Standard specifications require perforated bricks to have a minimum compressive strength of 7 MN/m² (approx 70 kg/cm²).

q: 24. The compressive strength of paving bricks should not be less than ............
explain: Paving bricks are subjected to heavy traffic wear, so they require a higher compressive strength of at least 40 MN/m².

q: 25. The length of a curved tile varies from ............
explain: Curved or pan tiles used for roofing generally have a standard length ranging from 15 cm to 20 cm as per sunil Sah Book and Geek Mcq But as per google option d .

q: 26. The commonly used raw material in the manufacture of cement, is ............
explain: Limestone provides the essential calcium carbonate (calcareous component) required for the production of Portland cement.
Dry rot is a fungal attack that consumes the wood's cellulose, eventually reducing the timber to a dry, brittle powder.

q: 28. In paints, the pigment is responsible for ............
explain: Pigments are finely ground solid particles that provide the paint with its specific colour and opacity.

q: 29. The percentage of alumina and silica in good fire clay vary respectively is ............
explain: Good fire clay typically contains approximately 25% Alumina and 75% Silica to withstand high temperatures without melting.

q: 30. For slaking of 10 kg of CaO, the theoretical amount of water is ............
explain: Theoretically, about 32% of the weight of CaO is required for the chemical reaction of slaking. For 10 kg, this is 3.2 kg of water.

q: 31. Pick up the compound responsible for early strength of cement from the following ............
explain: Tri-calcium silicate (C3S) hydrates quickly and is responsible for the high early strength of cement within the first 7 days.

q: 32. The percentage of the residue left after sieving good Portland cement in 90 micron sieve should not exceed ............
explain: Fineness of cement is checked using a 90-micron sieve; for OPC, the residue by weight should not exceed 10%.

q: 33. The expansion in Portland cement can be tested by ............
explain: The soundness test (using Le-Chatelier apparatus) measures the ability of cement to retain its volume and detects expansion caused by free lime.

q: 34. The compressive strength of a good Portland cement and standards and mortar after 3 days of curing should not be less than ............
explain: According to standard specifications, the minimum 3-day compressive strength of OPC mortar cubes is 11.5 MN/m².

q: 35. The sand is mixed with lime mortar to ............
explain: Sand acts as an inert filler in lime mortar to prevent excessive shrinkage and the resulting cracks during the setting process.

q: 36. Into how many units are all the rocks geologically classified?
explain: Geologically, rocks are classified into three categories: Igneous, Sedimentary, and Metamorphic.

q: 37. Which of the following rocks is used in cement manufacturing?
explain: Limestone is the primary calcareous material used to provide the lime (CaO) content in cement manufacturing.

q: 38. Plywood is normally available ............
explain: Common commercial plywood used for general purposes typically starts at a thickness of 3 mm to 4 mm.

q: 39. Plywood is made from ............
explain: Plywood is manufactured by gluing together thin layers (veneers) of Teak timber in alternating grain directions.

q: 40. Fibre boards can be ............
explain: As Per Key in Book option d but As per google Fibre boards have a smooth surface that allows for both painting and distempering for interior finishes.

q: 41. The most commonly used base for timber painting, is ............
explain: White lead is a widely used base for timber painting because it is durable and forms a flexible film that adjusts to the wood's movement.

q: 42. The commonly used base for iron and steel work, is ............
explain: Red lead is the most effective primer base for iron and steel because it provides excellent corrosion resistance.

q: 43. A volatile substance added to a paint to make its application easy and smooth, is known as ............
explain: Solvents (or thinners) are volatile liquids that reduce the viscosity of the paint to facilitate easy application.

q: 44. Most commonly used solvent in oil paints, is ............
explain: As Per Book Key of Sunil Sah And India Bix Site Petroleum is correct one  but Turpentine is the most common thinner/solvent used to adjust the consistency of oil-based paints. As of one comment in india bix Petroleum is the most commonly used solvent in oil paints. It is a good solvent because it dissolves the oil in the paint, evaporates slowly, and does not react with the paint. While other solvents can be used, petroleum is the preferred choice for most artists.So, the given answer is correct.

q: 45. Turpentine oil is used in paints as ............
explain: Turpentine acts as a thinner, reducing the thickness of the paint so it can be spread evenly.

q: 46. Linseed oil is used in paints as ............
explain: Linseed oil is a vehicle (or binder) that holds the pigment in suspension and forms a protective film on the surface.

q: 47. Varnish is a transparent or semi-transparent solution of resinous substances in ............
explain: Varnish can be prepared using alcohol (spirit varnish), linseed oil (oil varnish), or turpentine as the solvent for the resins.

q: 48. A bull nose brick is not used for ............
explain: Bull nose bricks have rounded corners and are used for aesthetics and safety on pillars or wall ends, but they are not used for structural arches.

q: 49. Second class bricks ............
options: produce a metallic sound when struck
explain: Second class bricks are reasonably well-burnt and should still produce a clear metallic ringing sound when struck together.

q: 50. Jhumb bricks are ............
explain: Jhumb bricks (or Jhama bricks) are over-burnt bricks. They are often vitrified, dark in colour, and used in foundation concrete.

q: 51. The portion of the brick cut across its width and having its length equal to that of a full brick, is known as ............
explain: A queen closer is a brick piece cut longitudinally into two equal halves. It has the same length as a full brick but half the width.

q: 52. The cracks which extend from bark towards the sap wood in the cross section of a tree, are called ............
explain: Star shakes are cracks that extend from the bark towards the sapwood. They are usually caused by severe frost or extreme heat during the growth of the tree.

q: 53. The cracks caused by shrinkage of the exterior surface of the wood exposed to atmosphere are called ............
explain: Wind cracks (or surface checks) occur when the outer layers of wood dry and shrink faster than the inner layers, causing the surface to rupture.

q: 54. The rocks formed due to solidification of molten mass laying below or above the earth surface are called ............
explain: Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling and solidification of molten rock (magma below the surface or lava above it).

q: 55. The sedimentary rocks are formed due to ............
options: solidification of molten mass lying below or above the earth surface
gradual deposition of materials like sand, clay, etc., generally by setting water
alteration of original structure under heat and excessive pressure
explain: Sedimentary rocks (also called aqueous rocks) are formed by the accumulation and lithification of mineral or organic particles deposited over time, often in water bodies.

q: 56. Spalling hammer is used for ............
explain: A spalling hammer is a heavy hammer used in the initial stage of stone dressing to knock off large, irregular chunks (spalls) from a quarry stone.

q: 57. The rock generally used for roofing, is ............
explain: Slate is a fine-grained, foliated metamorphic rock that can be easily split into thin, flat sheets, making it ideal for roofing shingles.

q: 58. Good quality stones must ............
explain: A good building stone should be durable against weathering, free from internal flaws like clay pockets, and resistant to atmospheric acids in industrial areas.

q: 59. The dolomite bricks are ............
explain: Dolomite bricks are refractory bricks used in furnace linings. Chemically, they are basic because they contain calcium and magnesium oxides.

q: 60. Quick lime is a ............
options: Product left immediately after the calcinations of pure limestone
explain: Quick lime (CaO) is the caustic product obtained by the calcination (heating) of limestone. Option 'b' is also chemically correct, but 'c' describes its production process as a material.

q: 61. After the addition of water to it, the cement sets and hardens due to ............
options: the heat produced by the chemical action
the hydration and hydrolysis of the constituent compounds of cement
explain: The hardening of cement is a chemical process involving hydration (reaction with water) and hydrolysis of its main compounds (C3S, C2S, C3A).

q: 62. The consistency test is performed to find ............
explain: The standard consistency test (using Vicat's apparatus) determines the percentage of water required to produce a cement paste of standard viscosity for other tests.

q: 63. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between ............
explain: Standard consistency is achieved when the Vicat plunger penetrates the paste to a point 5 to 7 mm from the bottom of the mold (which corresponds to 33-35 mm penetration from the top).

q: 64. In briquette test, the seven day tensile strength of good Portland cement should not be less than ............
explain: According to traditional tensile tests, the 7-day strength for standard OPC should be at least 2.5 N/mm² (roughly 25-30 kg/cm²).

q: 65. The seven day compressive strength of a good Portland cement, as obtained from the compressive test on cement-sand mortar cubes, should not be less than ............
explain: For standard OPC, the 7-day compressive strength should be at least 17.5 N/mm² (175 kg/cm²).

q: 66. The final setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be less than ............
explain: The final setting time for OPC should not exceed 10 hours (600 minutes) as per standard engineering specifications.

q: 67. Quick setting cement is used ............
options: for the construction of structures under water
where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick setting cement is essential for underwater work or running water conditions where the concrete must set before it is washed away.

q: 68. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are ............
explain: Quick setting cement has a very short initial setting time (5 minutes) and a final setting time of 30 minutes.

q: 69. The pozzolona portland cement gains the strength ............
options: in the same time as ordinary Portland cement
in less time than ordinary Portland cement
In more time than ordinary Portland cement
explain: PPC gains strength slower than OPC initially because the pozzolanic reaction takes longer to develop compared to the hydration of C3S.

q: 70. Compared to the ordinary Portland cement, the ultimate strength of the pozzolona Portland cement is ............
explain: Although PPC is slower to gain strength initially, its ultimate (long-term) strength is generally slightly higher than OPC.

q: 71. In low heat cement, the proportion of the following compound is kept at low value ............
explain: To reduce heat of hydration, the content of C3A (highest heat) and C3S (early heat) is minimized, while C2S is increased.

q: 72. A limestone found in seams of great thickness in non-crystalline texture with earthy appearance is called ............
explain: Compact limestone is the type of limestone found in seams of great thickness, characterized by a non-crystalline texture and an earthy appearance. It is a dense, hard stone often used in construction and for producing lime, differing from granular, magnesian, or kankar types. Compact Limestone: Non-crystalline, earthy, and found in large seams.Granular Limestone: Crystalline, granular texture (e.g., marble).Magnesian Limestone: Contains high amounts of magnesium carbonate.Kankar: Nodular, impure limestone found in soil.

q: 73. A limestone containing about 30% of alumina and silica is called ............
explain: Limestones with a high percentage of clay (alumina/silica) like Kankar are known as argillaceous limestones and produce hydraulic lime.

q: 74. The compressive strength of sandstone is ............
explain: Standard building-grade sandstone typically has a compressive strength around 65 MN/m² (approx 650 kg/cm²).

q: 75. The specific gravity of sandstone is ............
explain: Sandstone is relatively porous and light compared to igneous rocks, with a specific gravity generally falling between 2.65 and 2.95.

q: 76. High alumina cement is produced by fusing together a mixture of ............
options: limestone, gypsum, bauxite, clay and chalk
explain: High Alumina Cement (HAC) is manufactured by fusing a mixture of limestone (calcareous) and bauxite (aluminous) at very high temperatures.

q: 77. King closers are related to ............
explain: A king closer is a type of brick cut used in masonry where one corner is cut off so the width at one end is half the full width.

q: 78. Surkhi is added to lime mortar to ............
explain: Surkhi (ground burnt clay) is a pozzolanic material. When added to lime, it reacts to give the mortar hydraulic properties (ability to set in damp conditions).

q: 79. The role of super plasticizers in a cement paste is to ............
options: disperse the particles and to remove air bubbles
disperse the particles, removes air bubbles and to retard setting
explain: Superplasticizers (High Range Water Reducers) disperse cement particles to increase workability, help evacuate air, and often contain components to control setting time.

q: 80. In the cement the compound quickest to react with water, is ............
explain: Tri-calcium Aluminate (C3A) is the most reactive compound and is responsible for the 'flash set' if gypsum is not present.

q: 81. Rapid hardening cement contains ............
explain: Rapid hardening cement achieves strength quickly due to a higher proportion of Tri-calcium Silicate (C3S) and finer grinding.

q: 82. Generally wooden moulds are made from ............
explain: Sisham is often preferred over teak because it is generally more affordable while providing excellent longevity and stability, according to IndiaBIX and ZoneTech.

q: 83. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is ............
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous, permanent structure with a roof, allowing brick burning to continue even during the rainy season.

q: 84. The lime which contains mainly calcium oxide and slacks with water is ............
explain: Quick lime is nearly pure calcium oxide (CaO). When water is added, it undergoes the process of 'slaking'.

q: 85. Excess of silica in the clay ............
options: makers the brick brittle and weak
makes the brick crack and warp on drying
changes colour of the brick from red to yellow
improves impermeability and durability of the brick
explain: Silica prevents shrinkage, but if present in excess, it destroys the cohesion between clay particles, making the brick brittle.

q: 86. Which of the following constituent, when present in excess quantity in clay causes the bricks to melt and distort during burning?
explain: Excess lime acts as a flux during burning, causing the bricks to fuse, melt, and lose their shape.

q: 87. The alkaline salt present in the bricks, absorbs moisture from the air which on drying ............
options: leaves pores and makes the bricks porous
leaves high powder deposit on the brick
makes the bricks brittle and weak
explain: Alkalies cause 'efflorescence', where white powdery salt deposits appear on the surface of the brick after moisture evaporates.

q: 88. The good clay for making bricks is ............
explain: Weathering (exposure to atmosphere for several months) improves the plasticity and uniformity of the clay for brick making.

q: 89. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks, is known as ............
explain: As Per Book Key And Zone tech ,The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks is known as kneading.Tempering means converting of the prepared brick earth into a homogeneous mix of the desired plasticity by mixing it thoroughly with proper quantities of water.The process of working and tempering clay to make it plastic and of uniform consistency is known as pugging.

q: 90. The bricks after moulding should be dried in ............
options: air for 3 to 8 days but not in sun
explain: Bricks should be dried in the shade (protected from direct sun) to prevent uneven drying and cracking.

q: 91. The indentation marks left on bricks during the process of moulding, are known as ............
explain: The 'frog' is the depression on the top face of the brick. It serves as a key for mortar and often displays the manufacturer's name.

q: 92. The average out-turn of first class bricks in clamp burning is about ............
explain: Clamps are less efficient than kilns; typically only about 60% of bricks from a clamp are first-class quality.

q: 93. The average out-turn of first class bricks in kiln burning is ............
explain: Kilns offer better control over temperature, yielding a higher first-class brick out-turn of about 80-90%.

q: 94. Portland cement manufactured from pure white chalk and clay but free form iron-oxide, is known as ............
explain: Iron oxide gives cement its grey colour. White cement is made by using materials free from iron and manganese oxides.

q: 95. The percentage of water for normal consistency, is ............
explain: For most cements, the amount of water required for normal consistency (P) ranges between 25% and 35% of the weight of cement.

q: 96. If P is the percentage of water required for normal consistency, water to be added for determination of initial setting time, is ............
explain: Standard tests specify using 0.85P water for setting time and soundness (Le-Chatelier) tests.

q: 97. Soundness of cement is tested by ............
explain: The Le-Chatelier apparatus is specifically used to measure the expansion (soundness) of cement caused by free lime.

q: 98. Soundness test of cement determines ............
explain: Soundness refers to the ability of cement to maintain its volume. An 'unsound' cement expands due to excess free lime or magnesia.

q: 99. In a mortar, the binding material is ............
explain: Mortar consists of a binding material (like cement or lime) and an inert material/fine aggregate (like sand).

q: 100. Good quality sand is never obtained from ............
explain: Sea sand contains salts (chlorides) that absorb moisture (deliquescence) and cause corrosion in reinforcement and efflorescence in masonry.
